svg.text: C Standalone sub-mechanisms (2 of 2) — cutting and moving between vessels
Each panel loops on its own. Interposers, sleeves and rotating receivers turn a transfer into an operation.
source: C-universal-vessel.md section 5
S-14, S-17, S-18, S-20, S-24 are not drawn (control ideas or variants)
S-12 Undersized-die onion peeling
The halved onion, root and tip cut off, is pushed cut face first
through a die chosen by camera. Skin and the outermost layer are
stripped off as waste (20–30 % loss).
S-13 Three-layer inversion

g.text: 1 pot / strainer / empty pot, turned over
3 pasta drained in its own pot

svg.text: The solids never leave their pot, the cooking water is kept for
the sauce, and at no moment is there an open stream of boiling
water.
S-15 Spin-spread and cone-roll

g.text: cone roller, apex on the axis:

svg.text: A pan on a turntable spreads crêpe batter by rotation and rolls
dough to a round sheet of 2–10 mm, ±0.5 mm, under a conical
roller.
S-21 Wedge-and-core disc

g.text: wedges into the pot, core with seeds into the beaker

svg.text: An apple divider scaled up: the piston pushes the fruit through
6–8 blades round a core tube (1–2 kN). Cores apples, pears,
peppers; quarters cabbage round the stalk.
S-22 Ring-build and push-out

g.text: soft piston holds, fork lifts the sleeve
layers dosed into a ring on a base disc

svg.text: A sleeve on a base disc is the chef's ring mould: burger,
tiramisu, layered salad, gratin tower. Bake in it and it is a
spring-form tin.
S-23 Sickle carving in the stack
One slice per turn of the receiving pan; the fork lowers the
sleeve by 2–15 mm per turn. Slices fall flat into the warm pan.
Also bread, sausage, cooked potatoes.
